aspects.says: An Async method given no executor runs its callback on ForkJoinPool.commonPool(), not on the thread of the task that attached it.
basis: section:State Confined to One Thread Needs No Lock, Until a Callback Runs Somewhere Else

aspects.says: A callback attached with a non-async method runs on the thread that completes the future, or at once on the attaching thread when the future is already complete, so state confined to an owner thread must be handed back through the owner's executor.
basis: section:State Confined to One Thread Needs No Lock, Until a Callback Runs Somewhere Else

aspects.says: Calling another object's method while holding your lock adds its locks to your lock order, so two classes that each take only their own lock can deadlock.
basis: section:A Call to Another Object Under Your Lock Adds That Object's Locks to Your Lock Order

aspects.says: findDeadlockedThreads() reports cycles of monitors and of ReentrantLocks; findMonitorDeadlockedThreads() only monitors; neither sees a cycle through a Future.
basis: section:A Call to Another Object Under Your Lock Adds That Object's Locks to Your Lock Order
aspects.reason: a fact about a diagnostic API; the tank practice's tests use the detector, and the reader doesn't write detection code

aspects.says: @GuardedBy documents which lock guards a field; javac checks nothing, so a helper that needs the lock asserts it, and tests run with -ea catch an unguarded call.
basis: section:Write Down Which Lock Guards Each Field, and Let the Code Check It

aspects.says: An object passed between threads is either immutable or handed off by a sender that keeps no reference to it.
basis: section:What Passes Between Threads Is Immutable, or Its Sender Never Touches It Again

aspects.says: A latch remembers only what it is told: a loader that throws before countDown() leaves the waiter waiting until its timeout.
basis: section:A Latch or a Queue Remembers a Signal That wait() Can Miss

aspects.says: A local variable is confined to its thread only while the object it refers to isn't handed to another thread.
basis: section:State Confined to One Thread Needs No Lock, Until a Callback Runs Somewhere Else
aspects.reason: stated in one clause with a pointer to unit 4.4.4, whose parallel-stream practice checks it

aspects.says: notifyAll() wakes only threads already waiting and records nothing, while a latch keeps its count, so a signal sent before the wait is not lost.
basis: section:A Latch or a Queue Remembers a Signal That wait() Can Miss

aspects.says: An open call holds the lock only to change state and copy what the call needs, and makes the call after releasing it.
basis: section:A Call to Another Object Under Your Lock Adds That Object's Locks to Your Lock Order

aspects.says: A queue hands over a reference, and its put-to-take edge covers only writes made before the put, so a sender that changes the object afterwards corrupts what the consumer reads.
basis: section:What Passes Between Threads Is Immutable, or Its Sender Never Touches It Again

aspects.says: Reads of confined state run on the owner thread too, not only writes.
basis: section:State Confined to One Thread Needs No Lock, Until a Callback Runs Somewhere Else

aspects.says: Thread.holdsLock answers only for monitors; a ReentrantLock is checked with isHeldByCurrentThread(), and isLocked() is true when any thread holds it.
basis: section:Write Down Which Lock Guards Each Field, and Let the Code Check It
